title: Claude Code information-display evidence map
objective: Establish how current Claude Code decides between hidden, one-line, compact, and fully expanded presentation for thinking, tool calls, results, errors, long-running commands, permissions, background work, and tasks.

include: Official Anthropic Claude Code documentation and release notes
Locally available TypeScript baseline under ../src when present
Observable interaction contracts, keyboard toggles, truncation rules, and accessibility behavior
Per-command payload fields that are shown by default versus available on demand
exclude: Implementing changes in the Go project
Claims inferred only from marketing screenshots
Undocumented behavior without an explicit confidence label

deliverables: A source-backed behavior matrix covering lifecycle state, default density, expansion trigger, and retained evidence
Exact local TypeScript file/symbol references where available
A list of product-version or terminal-surface uncertainties
acceptance_criteria: Separates official documentation, source-code evidence, direct observation, and inference
Covers success, error, running, permission-required, and background states
Includes command-specific examples rather than a single global rule
verification: Every material product claim has a URL or repository file:line reference

result.summary: Source-backed Claude Code display behavior matrix with tool-specific, transcript, agent, permission, and accessibility evidence.
